Start settings not applied:
Squad activity
Runs the work steps of the activity the squad's planner picked; other activities run through the modules that already do them.
A fireteam lines up on the wall beside a door, waits until everyone is in line, holds fire, opens it, checks the doorway, and flows in to fanned corners.
Indoors with nothing in sight the squad clears the floor room by room: doorway, the far side of the room, a look round, and never two men in one room.
Car crew
A crew that owns a car: a pass with the windows down, a pull-up with the car as cover, a radio call for a second car, and getting out of there.
Careful relation
A faction that is careful with the player warns at range, warns again closer, and turns hostile when the warnings are walked through or shouted over.
Car ride
Walks a crew you offered a ride to your car and seats them.
Follows, holds and waits for the player who recruited this NPC.
Stealth killer
Shadows a person from behind, sneaking, and opens with a backstab at double damage. Picks locks instead of breaching.
Keeps distance, gives ground when the fight closes, and fires deliberate single shots.
Finds the group's wounded after a fight, walks over, and dresses their wounds with its own bandages.
Takes a hidden position, holds fire, and springs when the target walks in close.
Combat strafing (weave)
Shooters sidestep left and right while trading fire with people.
Squad members keep a couple of tiles of air between each other.
Use cover
Shooters get out of the line of fire to reload, break contact when hurt, and fight from behind walls.
Ranged flanking
Approach lanes and wings at range; in a stalled firefight one shooter runs to the side of the enemy while the rest keep them pinned with covering fire.
Fortify the building
A garrison boards up its own windows and doors from the inside, leaving its entrance clear.
Gunner (suppression fire)
A shooter that loses its line dumps the magazine into the last known position, full auto, spraying left and right.
Any rifle in a squad can lay steady covering fire on the enemy while a squadmate moves: bounding to cover or flanking.
Dress wounds
A wounded actor stops after the fight, bandages, and loses the limp and the bleeding.
Eats, drinks and smokes between fights; at night a stance-less squad may board up a house and stay till morning.
Squad leader
Keeps the group together, deploys it on contact and rallies it after losses. Orders never delay shooting; its death scatters the group.
Melee fighters step back and sideways between swings with their face to the enemy, back off from a press of zombies and step back in; tuned for pairs and groups.
Melee flanking pair
A fighter holding an axe cuts through doors and windows faster, and does it when checking a noise.
Intimidating approach
Walk up on a player at a walk, shout the warning from range, and only then close in to strike.
Cautious melee retreat
Retreat early when fewer zombies than usual close in, then come back in.
Hold the house at night
A house crew goes quiet after dark -- sits, eats, talks, ignores the dead outside -- wakes when a player comes to the walls, and clears the yard at dawn.

The squad stops, takes a nearby house or cover and idles with roles: one keeps watch, one sits, two talk, one comments, one stays quiet, others eat or smoke; then the route resumes. With group life off it stands in a circle instead.
a roof
rest at
A free group picks a goal, talks it over, walks there and sticks to it until it is done or too dangerous.
Radio call

An actor allowed to call backup goes to the group's radio on contact (running while the threat can see or reach him), works it for static and a short talk, then calls the faction's support. Kill him mid-call and none comes.
Robbery
An outlaw crew holds up a lone player: weapon down, hands up, three or four valuable items taken, then it leaves. Refusing gets him shot.
Works a nearby building end to end, falling back to loose containers.
After combat, search up to two bodies for a bounded share of non-clothing loot.
Encounter stance
Holds the post an encounter was spawned for: garrisons, roadblocks, routes, upper floors, a broken car.
Aimed movement
Shooters keep the gun on the target, or where it was last seen, while they walk.
Talk and presence
Answers a player who talks, greets without stopping, says a word when passing, and calls out a stranger when it is an outlaw crew.
Obeys hold/move orders issued by an admin or the director.
Investigate noises
Walks toward gunfire and other sounds it did not make.
Closes back up with the rest of the group when it drifts apart.
Shares one travel heading with the rest of the group.
Visitor life
A guest inside the house walks around, sits, reads, looks out of a window, washes and warms up.

A hostile crew may shout a warning and hold fire before it strikes, or open a standoff with questions. The player's reputation decides how many crews skip that and attack on sight: the worse the name, the more of them. Off means attack on sight, and a sandbox chance lets an Off crew warn anyway. Raid crews, assassins and ambushers ship Off.
ROTATE T
A squad prefers the target a squadmate just called, so fire lands on one enemy instead of spreading.
A shooter holds fire and sidesteps when a squadmate stands in the line of fire.
Switch to melee against zombies
On: a gun user may keep the gun stowed and use a melee weapon, shove or walk past zombies (the Combat Expert gun discipline). Off: the NPC uses the weapon it holds.
Rounds that crack past an NPC pin it down: worse aim, slower to shoot back, bursts held while pinned, and a push into cover.

An NPC that is not itself well armed backs away from a player or hostile who aims or raises a firearm: a per-NPC roll, then a run along a path that breaks line of sight, and a return to its goal once the gun has been out of sight for a few seconds. On by default for civilian, worker and rescue classes and melee crews.
Retreat from hordes
When the sandbox option is on, NPCs pull back once enough zombies are close by.
Panic on contact
The first sight of a person is a beat of disorder: a shout, a dash for cover or a freeze, near rounds pin, the leader steadies the line. Once per engagement, once per squad per minute; never zombies.
The badly wounded break off and a shaken gunman may rout; fear of guns belongs to the gun fear module.
Withdraw and re-engage
A losing shooter breaks contact, holes up out of sight, then comes back in from another side.
